issues.failure_explanation: The Gram matrix is first split as diag(B^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2) + offdiag(gamma B^T y). It is then rewritten as diag(B^TB, 1) + [[0, gamma B^T y],[gamma y^T B, gamma^2||x+y||^2]]. The (2,2) entry of that sum is 1+gamma^2||x+y||^2, so the rewriting is wrong. The proof also uses lambda_max(diag(B^TB,1)) <= sigma_max^2(B) and lambda_min(diag(B^TB,1)) >= sigma_min^2(B). In fact these eigenvalues are max(sigma_max^2,1) and min(sigma_min^2,1), so both claims fail in general. With the (2,2) entry corrected, the lower bound on sigma_min^2 does not hold. Counterexample: B=(1,0)^T, x=(0,1)^T, y=(1,0)^T, gamma=1, so [B,b]=[[1,1],[0,1]] and kappa=(3+sqrt5)/2≈2.618. The stated bound gives sqrt((4+sqrt8)/(4-sqrt8))≈2.414<2.618. The denominator can also be nonpositive, which is not excluded. Item 2 is derived from item 1. Its hypothesis ||B^Ty||/||x+y|| <= (eps^2-1)/4 also does not imply the step 'sqrt(1+4||B^Ty||^2/||x+y||^2) <= eps' that the proof uses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the eigenvalue estimates with a correct splitting, e.g. diag(B^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2) plus the off-diagonal part with eigenvalues ±gamma||B^Ty||. State the resulting bound with max/min of sigma(B) and gamma, and with a positive denominator. Then re-derive item 2 with a correct hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: Both the general bound (item 1) and the normalized-column bound with f(B,eps) (item 2) are unsupported and false as stated. The paper's claim to bound the growth for a non-orthonormal B is not established by this theorem.
issues.title: Condition-number bound of Theorem thm:cool is false: faulty splitting of the Gram matrix
issues.why_classification: The stated formulas must be replaced, and item 2 must be re-derived. A contained re-derivation with standard Weyl-type inequalities gives a comparable bound, so no new global architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: For alpha>0 the integral definition gives, as alpha->0, Q_M(0,beta)=Gamma(M,beta^2/2)/Gamma(M). Check with M=1: Q_1(0,beta)=e^{-beta^2/2}. The paper's alpha=0 definition gives Gamma(1,beta^2)=e^{-beta^2}. Equivalently, P(||Y||>eps)=P(chi^2_m>eps^2/sigma^2)=Gamma(m/2,eps^2/(2 sigma^2))/Gamma(m/2). The paper's definition lacks the factor 1/2 in the argument. So Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel at X=0 and Corollary cor:golden2 are false with the paper's definition of Q(0,.). Corollary cor:golden3 uses the same case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Gamma(M,beta^2) by Gamma(M,beta^2/2) in the alpha=0 case of the definition.
issues.overall_effect: All statements that evaluate Q^{ma}_M(0,.) are numerically wrong, as is the X=0 case of Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel. The case alpha>0, and hence the main results with X≠0, are unaffected.
issues.title: Marcum-Q at alpha=0 defined with the wrong incomplete-gamma argument, so the X=0 results are wrong
issues.why_classification: A one-term local correction restores all claims and no argument changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The degrees of freedom (m-n)/2 equal dim(span(B)^perp)/2 only if rank(B)=n. For B=0 (n>=1), P_B^perp(Y)=Y and the probability involves Q_{m/2}, not Q_{(m-n)/2}. For m=n and B of full rank, Q^{ma}_0 is undefined because the definition requires M>0. Theorem thm:projected-noise has the same m>=n boundary problem.

failure_location.quote: Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses 'B has full column rank' and 'm>n' (or treat m=n separately), and likewise for Theorem thm:projected-noise.
issues.overall_effect: The statement is false or undefined for rank-deficient B and for m=n.
issues.title: Corollary cor:golden3 omits full column rank (and m>n) needed for the dimension m-n
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypotheses is local and the substantive claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: No proof or computation is given, and X is arbitrary in span(Q^perp), so X=0 is allowed. Take X=0, m-n=100, sigma=2^{-8}. Then ||P^perp Y||^2=sigma^2 chi^2_100 and the event ||P^perp Y||>1/10 means chi^2_100>0.01*2^16≈655. The mean is 100 and the sd is about 14, so this probability is essentially 0, not >=0.9734. Reading the event as '<=' also fails: for large m-n the probability tends to 0, so no bound uniform over m-n>=100 exists.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the needed hypothesis on ||X|| (or give the intended event and direction), and derive the number from the Marcum-Q formula of Theorem thm:projected-noise.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised illustration that the probability is substantial for tall matrices is unsupported and false in general.
issues.title: Numerical lower bound 0.9734 in Corollary cor:added-1 is unsupported and false for X=0
issues.why_classification: The claim must be reformulated with extra hypotheses and a computation supplied, but the surrounding theory is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Z_1=||Y_1||_2 and Z_2=||X̄+Y_2||_2 are norms. Only Z_1^2/sigma^2 and Z_2^2/sigma^2 are (non)central chi-square. The noncentral F statistic is (Z_2^2/(m-n))/(Z_1^2/n). The event Z_2/Z_1 >= eps_2/eps_1 therefore corresponds to the F-argument n eps_2^2/((m-n) eps_1^2), not n eps_2/((m-n) eps_1). The theorem and the proof treat the unsquared ratio as F-distributed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use squared norms: replace the F-argument by n eps_2^2/((m-n) eps_1^2) and propagate it to the corollaries.
issues.overall_effect: The probability formula in Theorem thm:noise-ls is wrong, and the probability bounds of cor-main and cor:added-2 inherit the error.
issues.title: Theorem thm:noise-ls: F-distribution applied to norms instead of squared norms
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the argument, propagated verbatim, restores the intended result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof shows P(||r||>=threshold)=1-P(ratio<x), the survival function of the F-type ratio. It then equates this to F'_{m-n,n}(x;lambda), which is the CDF value if F' denotes the noncentral F distribution function. F' is never defined. With the CDF reading the theorem is false: as eps_1->0 the threshold tends to 1 and the true probability is P(P_Q Y=0)=0, while the CDF at infinity is 1. The statement also allows eps_1=0, where the argument n eps_2/((m-n) eps_1) is undefined. Cor. cor:added-2 uses F' as the probability of the good event.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define F' and write the probability as 1-F'(.) (or define F' as the survival function), restrict to eps_1>0, and propagate the change to the corollaries.
issues.overall_effect: The probability expression in Theorem thm:noise-ls, and the guarantees built on it, have the wrong direction (complement) unless F' is redefined. The case eps_1=0 is ill-defined.
issues.title: Theorem thm:noise-ls: survival probability identified with the F' value; F' undefined; eps_1=0 not handled
issues.why_classification: The fix is a routine local change of notation and direction, and the proof structure survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only uses [B,c gamma]=[Q,c] diag(R,gamma), which yields the second expression, with kappa([Q,c]). The first expression, with kappa([Q,c gamma]) and no gamma factors, would need [B,c gamma]=[Q,c gamma] diag(R,1), which the proof never uses. The two expressions are not equal. Example: B=e_1 in R^2, c=(1,1), gamma=2. The first gives kappa([e_1,2c])≈4.265, the second gives 2*kappa([e_1,c])≈5.236. Theorem lm:cond-ls uses the unproved first expression.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace '=' by separate inequalities and prove the first one from [B,c gamma]=[Q,c gamma] diag(R,1).
issues.overall_effect: The statement contains a false equality, and the form actually used downstream is not covered by the given proof.
issues.title: Theorem thm:min-max-cond item 3: equality between two different bounds; first bound not proved
issues.why_classification: The missing factorization argument is one routine line and every conclusion survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $r \neq 0$ is the residual of the least squares problem ($\|r\|_2 = \min_{u} \|c - Bu\|_2$).

issues.failure_explanation: In the cited theorem r is the residual for c, and the formula involves gamma||r||. Theorem lm:cond-ls defines r as the residual for c gamma, but still inserts the formula with gamma||r||, which is then off by a factor gamma. Example: B=e_1 in R^2, c=e_2, gamma=2. Then ||r||=2 for c gamma, alpha=5, and alpha^2-4 gamma^2||r||^2=25-64<0, so the bound is not even real. The case r=0 is also not excluded, although it is excluded in the cited theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define r as the residual of c (or replace ||r|| by ||r||/gamma) and add the hypothesis r≠0.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is wrong or ill-defined for gamma≠1. Corollaries cor:cond-ls and cor-main use gamma=1 and are unaffected by this defect.
issues.title: Theorem lm:cond-ls: residual r defined for c·gamma but the cited formula uses the residual of c
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition fixes the statement; the gamma=1 case that is actually used is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: On the event ||r||>=rho=1/sqrt(1+t^2) with t=eps_1/eps_2, monotonicity of (1+sqrt(1-r^2))/r gives the bound (1+sqrt(1-rho^2))/rho = t+sqrt(1+t^2). The corollary states eps_1*sqrt(1+t^2). These differ: for eps_2=1 and eps_1->0 the stated factor tends to 0, which would force kappa([B,q])<kappa(B). That is impossible, for example when B is orthonormal, since kappa([B,q])>=1=kappa(B).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor by eps_1/eps_2 + sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) in cor-main and cor:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The condition-number bound of cor-main, and the product bound of cor:added-2 built from it, are wrong.
issues.title: Corollary cor-main: wrong final factor from the monotonicity step
issues.why_classification: It is a routine algebra correction, and the corrected result keeps the same structure and probability.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \) with columns of norm 1, \( q\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), such that \( \|q\|_2=1 \).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes Corollary cor:cond-ls, which requires unit-norm columns of B and a unit vector q. Neither is assumed in cor-main, and q is never defined. In particular nothing links q to X+Y, nor r to the vector r of thm:noise-ls (which corresponds to q=(X+Y)/||X+Y||). Without unit-norm columns, Claim claim:added-2 fails and the bound does not follow.

failure_location.quote: Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that B has unit-norm columns and define q=(X+Y)/||X+Y||, verifying that its residual is the r of thm:noise-ls.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the corollary's inequality involves an undefined object, and its proof uses a result outside its hypotheses.
issues.title: Corollary cor-main omits unit-norm columns and the definition of q, needed to apply Cor. cor:cond-ls
issues.why_classification: The omitted hypotheses and definition are explicit and routine to add, and the argument is otherwise unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: At step i the matrix B=Q̂[:,1:i-1] has i-1 columns. Applying cor-main with n=i-1 gives F'_{m-i+1,i-1}, with argument (i-1)eps_2/((m-i+1)eps_1). The statement uses F'_{m-i,i}, which corresponds to i columns already present. The same F' defects as in thm:noise-ls (squares, direction) are also inherited.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use F'_{m-i+1,i-1} with matching argument and index eps_1, eps_2 by i; make explicit the conditioning on Q̂[:,1:i-1] in the union bound.
issues.overall_effect: The guaranteed probability in the corollary is not the one the proof's method yields.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-2: wrong degrees of freedom in the per-step probability (off by one)
issues.why_classification: An index shift and an explicit conditioning remark restore the claim, and the method and bound shape are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: at iteration $i$ for all $1 \leq i \leq n$, orthogonalization is subject to noise.
This offers a new perspective on understanding MGS without the usual restrictions on machine precision or the number of columns in the input matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims specific implications for MGS and an analysis free of restrictions on precision and column count. No MGS analysis appears anywhere. The only QR result, cor:added-2, is a stylized model with i.i.d. Gaussian perturbation e_i of fixed variance and an a_i assumed exactly orthogonal to the previous computed columns. It does not model MGS's rounding errors, and it is itself affected by the defects above.

failure_location.quote: with specific implications for the Modified Gram-Schmidt (MGS) algorithm

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the conclusion to say the results concern an idealized Gaussian-noise orthogonalization model and give only heuristic motivation for MGS.
issues.overall_effect: The scope claimed for the results (MGS, no assumptions on precision or number of columns) is not supported by the formal content.
issues.title: Conclusion overclaims implications for MGS and removal of precision restrictions
issues.why_classification: Weakening the prose removes the overclaim without changing any theorem.
